reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a periodic square-wave pulse train with robust-standardized amplitude ranging from 0.0 (baseline) to approximately 2.47 (upper extreme), matching the catalog’s amplitude_90 value. The fundamental period is consistently ~98 points across all candidates, as confirmed by window_cycles: candidate 0 shows exactly 1 cycle in 98 points; candidates 1 and 2 show 3 cycles in 294 points (98 per cycle); candidate 3 shows 5 cycles in 490 points (98 per cycle). Pulses are near-vertical rising/falling edges (near-zero rise/fall time), flat tops at ~2.47, and flat baselines at 0.0. No measurable noise or jitter is present—edges align precisely to integer indices, and plateaus are perfectly horizontal. Baseline stability is absolute: median = 0.0, MAD = 0.0, roughness = 0.0, curvature = 0.0 across all references. Minor trend differences exist (slope_per_point: 0.0, +0.0084, 0.0, −0.0051) but are negligible relative to pulse magnitude and do not affect morphology; they likely stem from global drift in the underlying raw series, not local anomaly. All pulses are symmetric in width (~20–22 points high, ~76–78 points low), and no truncation occurs at boundaries—the first and last pulses are fully captured within each window. Acceptable variation includes tiny slope offsets (<0.01 per point) and exact pulse timing shifts due to global index offset; unacceptable deviations would include altered amplitude, non-rectangular shape, baseline offset, edge smearing, or irregular inter-pulse spacing.
